scenario_scope: Primary-source intake of coding-assistant work surfaces and freestanding agent runtimes as external implementation comparators for the evolution from bounded conversational help through agent harnesses to project, role, team, and organizational work.

cases.decision_rationale: elizaOS supplies a concrete modular runtime and scenario-runner comparator, while runtime authority, evidence qualification, and promotion already have explicit owners in the existing book.
required_before_drafting: review the official repository at a pinned commit
review canonical core-runtime, scenario-runner, security, and sandbox documentation
separate implemented project surfaces from the shared ChatGPT review's unverified diagnoses
evidence_transition_preconditions: run a claim-specific local or independently reviewed comparison
retain exact version, configuration, failures, costs, and boundary conditions
promotion_blockers: no local elizaOS execution or scenario reproduction
no independent security or performance assessment
non_claims: does not import reported project behavior into the ASI Stack
does not establish runtime safety, readiness, or state of the art
does not justify a new paper-shaped chapter

cases.decision_rationale: Hermes Agent provides a concrete skill-learning, persistent-memory, session-search, approval, and isolation comparator; those mechanisms fit established memory and runtime owners rather than a standalone product chapter.
required_before_drafting: review the official repository at a pinned commit
review canonical skills, memory, security, and architecture documentation
distinguish agent-authored procedures from validated or promoted capabilities
evidence_transition_preconditions: execute a claim-specific procedure-learning or memory-integrity comparison
measure proposal quality, regression, rollback, poisoning, and human-review costs
promotion_blockers: no reproduced learning, memory, security, or utility result
non_claims: does not equate skill mutation with safe self-improvement
does not establish memory correctness or command safety
does not justify a new paper-shaped chapter

cases.decision_rationale: OpenClaw supplies concrete gateway, session, ACP harness, policy, audit, and governed self-learning surfaces. It complements rather than duplicates the existing Claw-SWE-Bench evaluation source and fits four established lifecycle owners.
required_before_drafting: review the official repository at a pinned commit
review canonical gateway, agent-loop, ACP, sandbox-policy, memory, and self-learning documentation
keep the OpenClaw implementation source distinct from the Claw-SWE-Bench benchmark source
evidence_transition_preconditions: run a version-pinned claim-specific gateway, session, policy, or learning comparison
retain failures, policy configuration, identity joins, costs, and unresolved residuals
promotion_blockers: no reproduced security, reliability, learning, or benchmark result
non_claims: does not transfer Claw-SWE-Bench results to OpenClaw or the ASI Stack
does not establish ACP harness confinement or end-to-end authority correctness
does not justify a new paper-shaped chapter

cases.decision_rationale: GitHub Copilot, Augment, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Oh My Pi provide dated implementation landmarks for a distinct architectural question: how AI systems absorb progressively larger work surfaces by acquiring context, persistence, tools, execution custody, and review loops. Existing runtime and organizational chapters govern effects and delegation but do not own this transition model.
required_before_drafting: review each official product or repository source at an identified revision or access date
separate product documentation from reproduced behavior
use products as representative landmarks rather than a leaderboard or exhaustive market history
evidence_transition_preconditions: freeze one work-surface transition and matched workload
measure context transfer, completion, intervention, authority, effect, recovery, and cost outcomes
promotion_blockers: no common harness workload or organizational deployment
no causal evidence that one surface or stage is generally superior
non_claims: does not claim a universal linear chronology
does not predict that every role will be automated
does not rank the named products

cases.decision_rationale: Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and elizaOS remain mapped to their mechanism owners but also mark the move from repository-bound harnesses toward persistent, channel-connected, modular, and freestanding agents. The new chapter owns the cross-stage transition; the established chapters retain memory, effects, accountability, and societal deployment.
required_before_drafting: preserve existing source limits and constructive project-specific language
state that stages branch and coexist rather than replace one another
treat organization-wide autonomy as a governed design space and stress case
evidence_transition_preconditions: execute a bounded cross-surface or cross-runtime comparison
retain exact identities, permissions, effects, interventions, failures, and residuals
promotion_blockers: no reviewed project was executed for this intake
no role-level or organization-level substitution result exists
future pathways are architectural branches, not forecasts
non_claims: does not transfer project claims into the ASI Stack
does not equate persistence with accountability
does not establish autonomous organizations as desirable or inevitable

validation_boundary: Records primary-source routing for nine public software and product comparators plus one distinct cross-family chapter owner. It does not reproduce the products, import reported results, establish a universal history, forecast role replacement, or move any claim support state.
non_claims: does not treat chapter creation as evidence
does not add a Lean proof result
does not authorize deployment, release, or claim promotion
